**Safety parts we’ll add for the chatbot‑booking feature**

| Part | What it means |
|------|---------------|
| **Logins with email (magic link)** | Users sign in with a link sent to their inbox. No passwords, no store of credentials. |
| **AI calls on the server only** | The OpenAI key lives on the server (in Supabase function or Edge API), never in the browser. |
| **Per‑user confirmation for actions** | The bot will say “I am going to book an appointment on X at Y. Confirm?” so the user can stop it if it’s wrong. |
| **Bookings stored in Supabase** | A new table `appointments` with RLS rules: a user can only see or change their own appointments. |
| **Spending cap & rate limit** | We’ll set a low‑cost limit on how many AI calls a user can trigger per day to avoid overspending. |
| **Hidden secret keys** | The OpenAI key goes into Supabase secrets, not the code. |

---

### Starter questions (amber – extra safety needed)

1. **Who will use the chatbot?** (Everyone on the site, or just registered users?)
2. **What exact booking details do we need?** (Date, time, service type, any notes?)
3. **Do we already have a calendar / availability system?** (e.g. Google Calendar, Calendly, or the app should create free slots?)
4. **Do you want to send a confirmation email to the customer after booking?** (If yes, you’ll need an email‑sending service set up.)

When you reply, I’ll draft a one‑screen plan. If you’re okay with the safety defaults above, I can skip the questions and jump straight to the plan. Let me know!
